assessments.reasoning: The April 1969 first-printing notice gives the edition. Section 2.14.2 p. 2-14 describes LIBRA SAVE for saving a program to disk with a one- to four-character identifier in the multi-user extension. The section footnote marks it incomplete, and Table 4-1 at p. 4-13 marks the LIBRA segment as unimplemented at that point.

challenge.method: Compared the segment’s apparent present-tense implementation language with both limiting footnotes, the hardware context, and the January 1970 manual’s later availability statement on p. vii.
challenge.results: The two explicit April 1969 limitations govern the account of completion. They support an unfinished design, with the described syntax as an intended command. The later availability reference concerns a distinct printing and does not establish shipped command semantics in April 1969.

limitations: Evidence covers the named multi-user extension design from the April 1969 printing. No implementation test or release-date inference was performed.
